claims.text: Question-level hallucinations cannot be effectively identified through self-consistency checking alone.
Model-level hallucinations cannot be effectively identified through self-consistency checking alone.
SAC3 leverages semantically equivalent question perturbation to detect question-level hallucinations.
SAC3 leverages cross-model response consistency checking to detect model-level hallucinations.

evidence.description: Re-examination of existing detection approaches based on LM self-consistency uncovers question-level hallucinations that self-consistency alone cannot identify.
Re-examination of existing detection approaches based on LM self-consistency uncovers model-level hallucinations that self-consistency alone cannot identify.
The proposed SAC3 framework incorporates semantically equivalent question perturbation mechanisms to detect question-level hallucinations.
The proposed SAC3 framework incorporates cross-model response consistency checking mechanisms to detect model-level hallucinations.

methodologies.name: Semantic-aware Cross-check Consistency (SAC3)
methodologies.description: A sampling-based hallucination detection method expanding on self-consistency by integrating semantically equivalent question perturbation and cross-model response consistency checking.

limitations.text: Existing hallucination detection approaches relying solely on LM self-consistency fail to effectively identify question-level and model-level hallucinations.
